comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C95-C96 regarding astrocytic engulfment. Both evaluations support the finding that caspase-3 deficiency does not affect astrocytic synapse engulfment, with peer reviewers explicitly endorsing that caspase-3 is essential for microglial but not astrocytic synapse elimination.

Both address claims C118-C119 regarding caspase-3 upregulation in AD model. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to stochastic nature and limited temporal resolution, while peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED without raising concerns. This represents a disagreement in confidence level about the consistency of this finding.

Strong agreement on claims C76-C89 regarding electrophysiological evidence for defective circuit refinement in Casp3-/- mice. Both evaluations find the data convincing and support the conclusion that caspase-3 deficiency impairs weak synapse elimination. OpenEval includes C2 which peer review addresses separately.

Strong agreement on claims C4, C20, C110-C117 regarding caspase-3-mediated synapse loss in AD model. Both evaluations support the finding that caspase-3 deficiency prevents Aβ-induced synapse loss independent of amyloid clearance. OpenEval includes additional methodological claims C107-C109 not specifically addressed by peer review.

Agreement on claims C121-C122 regarding the overall mechanistic model. Both evaluations support the synthesized model of caspase-3-dependent synapse elimination. Peer review R10 also includes C101 which OpenEval addresses in R7.

Substantial agreement on claims C3, C19, C91-C94 regarding reduced synaptic engulfment by microglia in Casp3-/- mice. Both evaluations support this as a central finding. Peer review R5 also includes claims C97-C100 which OpenEval addresses separately in R7.

Strong agreement on claims C2, C61-C65, C71 regarding defective eye-specific territory segregation in Casp3-/- mice. Both evaluations support the quantitative data from Figure 3. OpenEval includes additional control claims C66-C70 which peer review addresses separately in R8.

Strong agreement on claims C1, C18, C34-C43, C47 regarding TeTxLC-mediated synapse inactivation leading to caspase-3 activation. Both evaluations find the evidence convincing. OpenEval includes additional methodological claims C27-C33 and controls C44-C46 not specifically mentioned in peer review.

Agreement on claims C56-C59 regarding differential caspase-3 activation in competitive interaction experiments. Both evaluations support this finding. OpenEval includes additional context claims C53-C55 and C60 not specifically addressed by peer review, which accepts this as part of the overall convincing evidence.

Partial overlap on claims C3, C97-C100 regarding preferential microglial engulfment of inactive synapses. Both evaluations support this finding. OpenEval R7 focuses on TeTxLC-induced engulfment experiments with claim C101, while peer R5 groups these with the broader microglial engulfment findings including C19, C91-C94.

Partial overlap on claims C66-C70 regarding control experiments ruling out neuronal death. OpenEval R3 includes these as controls for the segregation defect findings, while peer R8 implicitly accepts them as supporting evidence for localized, non-apoptotic caspase-3 function without specific critique.

OpenEval R10 addresses claims C48-C52 regarding mechanistic speculation about localized versus whole-cell caspase-3 activation, rating them as UNCERTAIN. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these speculative mechanistic claims about transitional states.

OpenEval R11 addresses claims C5-C17, C21-C26, C72-C75, C90, C102-C106 as established literature context, rating them as SUPPORTED. Peer review does not separately evaluate these background/contextual claims from prior literature.
